title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 79-81). Grothendieck works in a ⊗-additive category P_1 equipped with 'polynomial maps': P_n(X;M) for homogeneous maps of degree n, and multi-degree versions P_ν(X_1,…,X_r;M). He postulates representing objects Γ^n X, with universal degree-n maps e_n = γ_n : X → Γ^n X, so that P_n(X;M) ≅ P_1(Γ^n X, M). This abstracts Roby's theorem that divided powers represent homogeneous polynomial laws. On p.79 he also assumes P^⊗_ν(X_1..X_r;M) ≅ P_{1..1}(Γ^{ν_1}X_1,…,Γ^{ν_r}X_r;M) and derives the exponential formula Γ^n(X_1×…×X_r) ≅ ⊕_{|ν|=n} Γ^{ν_1}X_1⊗…⊗Γ^{ν_r}X_r, together with the unit X⊗1 ≅ X.

This page:
(1) X ↦ Γ^*(X) = (Γ^i X)_{i≥0} is a functor P_1 → Grad(P_1). It is not additive, but it is exponential: it sends ⊕ to ⊗, i.e. it is a symmetric monoidal functor (P_1,⊕) → (Grad P_1,⊗).
(2) Every object is a commutative group object for ⊕, via the codiagonal X⊕X → X and 0 → X. A symmetric monoidal functor carries commutative monoids to commutative monoids. Hence each Γ^*(X) gets a commutative graded ⊗-algebra structure, functorial in X: the divided-power algebra multiplication Γ^aX⊗Γ^bX → Γ^{a+b}X. The diagonal would likewise give a coalgebra and the antipode a Hopf structure; he does not say this.
(3) Plethysm maps (*) α^X_{p,q} : Γ^{pq}(X) → Γ^p(Γ^q(X)). They correspond, by the universal property, to the degree-pq map X → Γ^p(Γ^q X) obtained as the composite e_p^{Γ^q X} ∘ e_q^X of a degree-q map and a degree-p map. Classically this is γ_{pq}(x) ↦ γ_p(γ_q(x)), the universal form of the PD axiom γ_p(γ_q x) = (pq)!/(p!(q!)^p) γ_{pq}(x).
(4) Associativity (**): Γ^p(α_{q,r}) ∘ α_{p,qr} = α^{Γ^r X}_{p,q} ∘ α_{pq,r} as maps Γ^{pqr}X → Γ^pΓ^qΓ^r X. This holds automatically because both sides represent the composite degree-pqr map e_p∘e_q∘e_r.
(5) Unit conditions use Γ^1 = id and Γ^0 = 1.

The left margin seems to say that for the basic example (modules) these structures give the usual divided-power algebras.

The next page reverses the logic. One takes as axioms an exponential functor Γ^* : (P_1,⊕) → (P_1^{gr},⊗) with Γ^0 = 1 and Γ^1 = id, plus natural transformations α : Γ^{pq} → Γ^p∘Γ^q satisfying associativity and unit laws. This is an intrinsic 'divided-power/plethystic structure' on a ⊗-additive category, from which polynomial maps can be recovered. The purpose in the dossier, on multiplicative structures on ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes, is presumably to have an abstract framework for divided powers and symmetric powers (λ/γ-operations) on perfect complexes and their K-theory.
errors: No real error. Calling every object a 'groupe comm.' is more than needed: the commutative monoid structure from ⊕ already gives the commutative algebra. The group structure would add an antipode, making Γ^*(X) a commutative and cocommutative Hopf algebra, which he does not state.
Associativity (**) is automatic in the representable setting of this page, since both composites represent e_p∘e_q∘e_r. It becomes a genuine axiom only in the converse setting of p.81.
Commutativity of Γ^*(X) presupposes the symmetry constraint of Grad(P_1) without Koszul signs; this is not stated.

ideas.what: Γ^n as the object representing homogeneous degree-n polynomial maps, P_n(X;M) ≅ Hom(Γ^n X, M), axiomatized in a ⊗-additive category
ideas.modern_name: Roby's universal property of divided powers; representability underlying strict polynomial functors (Γ^d P)
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (1963) for modules; Friedlander–Suslin (1997) for strict polynomial functors

ideas.what: Γ^* is an exponential functor (⊕ → ⊗), so each Γ^*(X) is a commutative graded algebra, functorial in X
ideas.modern_name: exponential functor / symmetric monoidal functor (⊕,⊗); divided-power algebra Γ(X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Roby, Cartan); 'exponential functor' terminology from Franjou–Lannes–Schwartz, Touzé

ideas.what: Natural plethysm maps α_{p,q}: Γ^{pq} → Γ^p∘Γ^q with associativity and unit laws
ideas.modern_name: universal form of the PD axiom γ_p(γ_q x) ∝ γ_{pq}(x); plethysm/composition maps of strict polynomial functors (cf. PD-monads, Fresse's Γ(P))
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Cartan, Roby) for modules; categorical versions later

ideas.what: Converse: an exponential functor plus plethysm maps as an intrinsic 'divided power structure' on a ⊗-additive category (p.81)
ideas.modern_name: divided powers in symmetric monoidal / tensor categories
ideas.usually_credited_to: scattered later work (operadic divided powers, Fresse 2000; divided powers in symmetric tensor categories in positive characteristic)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets out to axiomatize 'divided power structures' on an abstract ⊗-additive category. The axioms are an exponential functor Γ^* : (P_1,⊕) → (Grad,⊗) with Γ^0 = 1, Γ^1 = id, plus plethysm transformations Γ^{pq} → Γ^p∘Γ^q satisfying associativity and unit. He clearly intends to recover a theory of polynomial maps from these data. This intrinsic, category-level characterization predates strict polynomial functors and later work on divided powers in tensor categories. It does not appear in his published or circulated texts.
missed.quote: X ↦ Γ^*(X) … est un foncteur (pas même additif !) … 'transformant sommes en ⊗' … Γ^p(Γ^q(X)) ⟵ Γ^{pq}(X) … condition 'd'associativité'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Divided powers in symmetric tensor categories (positive characteristic, Deligne-type categories) and derived divided powers are active topics. An axiomatization by exponential functor plus plethysm, with an equivalence to 'polynomial maps', is a natural but not standard framework. It is modest and close to known material, though.

deep.surprise_reason: Clean categorical axiomatization of divided powers (Roby representability, exponential functor, plethysm associativity) in an abstract ⊗-additive category around 1975, anticipating strict polynomial functors in spirit. The individual facts are classical, so this is an unpublished framework rather than a new theorem.
transcription_corrections: Margin note: legible fragments suggest it says that for the basic category (modules) 'ces structures de ⊗-algèbres' are the usual 'algèbres à puissances divisées', with a reference '2' (possibly to an annex). The exact wording is uncertain.
'On a défini[?] aussi[?] homs' is uncertain; it may read 'On a de plus des homs, fonctoriels en X'.
The struck word before '{+des P_1+}' is illegible. It is attached to the inserted phrase 'des P_1' and is not an independent statement.
In the composite, the labels are e_q^X (hom. de degré q) and e_p^{Γ^q(X)} (hom. de degré p), as transcribed. 'ce qui revient au même, un hom. de degré pq X → Γ^p(Γ^q(X))' is correct.
